correctness.rationale: Connectedness yields absorption with probability one. Exact rational first-step equations give mean \(2^{-n}\boldsymbol 1^{\mathsf T}(I-Q)^{-1}\boldsymbol 1\). A standalone full enumeration of every marked-edge connected graph at \(n\le 4\) gives exactly 0,1,6 addition orbits for \(n=2,3,4\). All 18 four-node rational deltas and the five-node LD star witness are independently recomputed by rational matrix calculations; the sign table yields exact minimal onsets of 4,4,5 for VM,IP,LD. No higher-order exhaustion is claimed.

originality.rationale: The method and larger-scale edge dependence are established in arXiv:1404.6360, but its finite paw illustration and fixed-edge-size maxima do not imply the exact rule-specific minimum insertion orders under fair independent starts. No reviewed source or actual semantic/query search returned the complete six-orbit sign table or five-agent LD onset. This is a best-knowledge claim with explicitly stated residual risk.
residual_risks: No finite collection of literature queries establishes universal absence of an unpublished or unindexed four-/five-agent exact census.
The same four-node paw and exact first-step method appear in arXiv:1404.6360; novelty is solely the new exact edge-insertion census and rule-specific sharp cutoff, not its computational technique.
Comparison relies on a specified i.i.d. fair initial law and per-attempt time; literature with balanced-only starts or event-rate normalization must be translated before asserting implication.

value.rationale: The monotonic effect of social-link additions on consensus time is a natural model-design question. The new exact complete first slowdown layer distinguishes three canonical update protocols, exposes an explicit same-edge reversal, and identifies a sharp five-participant boundary for the remaining protocol. A motivated minimal cutoff and exhaustive finite classification are useful even without an infinite-family theorem.
